'''Jai Pal Mittal''' (born 21 September 1940) is an Indian scientist, [[Department of Atomic Energy|DAE]] [[Raja Ramanna]] Fellow of [[Bhabha Atomic Research Centre]] and Distinguished Professor of [[Indian Institute of Technology, Mumbai]], the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] and the [[University of Pune]].<ref name="Biographical Sketch of Dr. Jai Pal Mittal">{{cite journal | title=Biographical Sketch of Dr. Jai Pal Mittal | author=Tulsi Mukherjee | journal=Res. Chem. Intermed. | year=2005 | volume=31 | issue=1–3 | pages=3–5 | doi=10.1163/1568567053146968| s2cid=97735658 }}</ref><ref name="INSA">{{cite web | url=http://insaindia.org.in/detail.php?id=N88-0997 | title=INSA | publisher=Indian National Science Academy | date=2015 | access-date=6 February 2015 | url-status=usurped | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160812230057/http://insaindia.org.in/detail.php?id=N88-0997 | archive-date=12 August 2016 | df=dmy-all }}</ref> He is known for his researches in the fields of [[photochemistry]] and [[radiation chemistry]].<ref name="ResearchGate Bio">{{cite web | url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Jai_Mittal2/info?awardsAction=scroll | title=ResearchGate | date=2015 | access-date=6 February 2015}}</ref> He was honoured by the [[Government of India]] in 2003 with [[Padma Shri]], the fourth highest Indian civilian award.<ref name="Padma Awards">{{cite web |url=http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf |title=Padma Awards |publisher=Padma Awards |date=2015 |access-date=6 February 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151015193758/http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf |archive-date=15 October 2015 }}</ref>

==Biography==
Jai Pal Mittal was born on 21 September 1940 in [[Meerut]] in the Indian state of [[Uttar Pradesh]].<ref name="Biographical Sketch of Dr. Jai Pal Mittal" /> He completed his graduate (BSc) and master's studies (MSc) in chemistry from the Agra University<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="ResearchGate Bio" /> and migrated to Mumbai in 1959, looking for career opportunities.<ref name="Biographical Sketch of Dr. Jai Pal Mittal" /> He joined the Training School of Atomic Energy Establishment, erstwhile [[Bhabha Atomic Research Centre]] and did a one-year course after which he moved to USA to join the Department of Radiation Chemistry of the [[University of Notre Dame]], Indiana.<ref name="Biographical Sketch of Dr. Jai Pal Mittal" /><ref name="INSA" /><ref name="ResearchGate Bio" /> He completed his doctoral studies (PhD) in 1967, under the guidance of A. A. Lamola and W. H. Hamill.<ref name="Biographical Sketch of Dr. Jai Pal Mittal" /> Receiving an invitation from [[Willard Libby]], the 1960 Nobel laureate in Chemistry, to assist him, Mittal did his post doctoral research, for over a year, at the Radiation and Nuclear Chemistry laboratory of the [[University of California]].<ref name="Biographical Sketch of Dr. Jai Pal Mittal" /><ref name="INSA" /><ref name="ResearchGate Bio" />

In 1969, Mittal returned to India to start his career as a Pool Officer at the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) and started working in the field of photochemistry.<ref name="Biographical Sketch of Dr. Jai Pal Mittal" /> Two years later, in 1971, he got an opportunity to work with Professor E. Hayon at the [[United States Army Natick Soldier Research, Development and Engineering Center]] and worked there for one year.<ref name="Biographical Sketch of Dr. Jai Pal Mittal" /> On his return to India in 1972, he formed a research group at BARC for research in photochemistry and radiation chemistry.<ref name="Biographical Sketch of Dr. Jai Pal Mittal" /> During this period, he organized the first national symposium in [[Thiruvananthapuram]], ''National Symposium on Fast Reaction Chemistry and Techniques''.<ref name="Biographical Sketch of Dr. Jai Pal Mittal" />

Mittal continued at BARC to become the Director of Chemistry and Isotope Group and the [[Department of Atomic Energy|DAE]] [[Raja Ramanna]] Fellow of the institution.<ref name="INSA" /> He also holds the position of M. N. Saha Distinguished Professor of the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]]<ref name="ResearchGate">{{cite web | url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Jai_Mittal2 | title=Profile on ResearchGate | date=2015 | access-date=6 February 2015}}</ref> and the post of a Distinguished Professor at the [[University of Pune]] and the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Mumbai]].<ref name="INSA" /> During his tenure at BARC, he is known to have contributed for the establishment of a ''nanosecond LINAC based pulse radiolysis system'' at BARC and promoted the ''nano, pico and femtosecond pump and probe techniques'' to study the chemical dynamics.<ref name="INSA" /> He is reported to have initiated a new school of research in Radiation Chemistry and Photochemistry in India<ref name="ResearchGate" /> and his group was successful in isotopic enrichment of hydrogen, carbon and uranium isotopes.<ref name="INSA" /> His research findings have been recorded by way of over 300 scientific papers,<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="ResearchGate Bio" /> published in peer reviewed journals and [[ResearchGate]], an online scientific data repository, have listed 250 of them.<ref name="ResearchGate" /> He has also mentored many students in their doctoral studies.<ref name="INSA" />

Mittal has been associated with the Board of Research in Nuclear Sciences as a chairman of many of its basic sciences committees. He is a former president of the Indian Society of Radiation and Photochem Sciences (1997-2001), the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] (2003–04)<ref name="ResearchGate Bio" /><ref name="NASI President">{{cite web | url=http://nasi.nic.in/pastprez.htm | title=NASI President | publisher=NASI | date=2015 | access-date=6 February 2015}}</ref> and the Asian Photochemistry Association (2003- 2008).<ref name="INSA" /> He has also served the [[Indian National Science Academy]] as a council member (1998-2000) and as an additional member (2005–06).<ref name="INSA" /> He serves as the president of the Asian and Oceanian Photochemistry Association<ref name="Asian and Oceanian Photchemistry Association">{{cite web | url=http://asianphotochem.com/member/members05_07.html | title=Asian and Oceanian Photchemistry Association | publisher=Asian and Oceanian Photchemistry Association | date=2015 | access-date=6 February 2015}}</ref> and is a member of the education council of the [[University of Allahabad]].<ref name="UoA">{{cite web | url=http://www.allduniv.ac.in/old/index.php?option=com_k2&view=item&id=205:members&Itemid=556 | title=UoA | publisher=University of Allahabad | date=2015 | access-date=6 February 2015}}</ref> He is a life member of the [[Indian Chemical Society]]<ref name="ResearchGate Bio" /> where has also been a past president.<ref name="INSA" />

Mittal lives in [[Navi Mumbai]] in [[Maharashtra]]<ref name="INSA" /> and continues attending seminars and conferences to deliver keynote addresses.<ref name="NASI lecture">{{cite web | url=http://nasi.nic.in/pjc_review.htm | title=NASI lecture | publisher=National Academy of Sciences | date=2015 | access-date=6 February 2015}}</ref>

==Awards and recognitions==
Jai Pal Mittal is an elected fellow the [[Indian National Science Academy]], [[National Academy of Sciences, India]],<ref name="NASI Fellow">{{cite web | url=http://nasi.nic.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=M | title=NASI Fellow | publisher=NASI | date=2015 | access-date=6 February 2015}}</ref> [[The World Academy of Sciences]], the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]]<ref name="Indian Academy of Sciences">{{cite web | url=http://www.ias.ac.in/php/fell_all.php3?alpha=M | title=Indian Academy of Sciences | publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences | date=2015 | access-date=6 February 2015}}</ref> and the [[Maharashtra Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="Biographical Sketch of Dr. Jai Pal Mittal" /><ref name="INSA" /> He is a recipient of two awards, Professor T. R. Seshadri 70th Birthday Commemoration Medal in 1994 and the Golden Jubilee Commemoration Medal in 2001, from the Indian National Science Academy.<ref name="INSA" /> A winner of 1964 Fulbright scholarship and 2002 Humboldt Research Award, Mittal has received the Senior JSPS Award, [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] N. R. Dhar Memorial Medal, Goyal Gold Medal and the [[Indian Science Congress Association]] Platinum Jubilee Award.<ref name="INSA" /> The [[Government of India]] awarded him the civilian award of [[Padma Shri]] in 2003.<ref name="INSA" /><ref name="ResearchGate Bio" />
